summary.headline: Gulf Oil Q2 FY27 core lubricant volume up 16% to 47,000 KL, revenue up 44%, EBITDA up 37%, margin 11.8% just below 12-14% band.
summary.overview: Gulf Oil reported Q2 FY27 volume growth of about 16% (core lubes 47,000 KL vs 40,500 KL) and revenue growth of 44%, with EBITDA up 37% YoY. EBITDA margin was 11.8%, close to the guided 12-14% band, and management said per-litre margins were protected despite input cost inflation from crude and base oil. Working capital rose in absolute terms on higher prices, though days stayed within the 95-105 day band. A fire at Valsad cost about 4-5 days of production, which is insured.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 slightly lower on monsoon; H1 roughly flat
vs INR 321 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: INR 109 crore in Q1 FY27; INR 88 crore in Q2 FY27
financial_highlights.change: vs insignificant amounts in prior four quarters

segments.name: Lubricants - OEM and franchisee workshops
segments.commentary: OEM factory fill grew double digit and OEM franchisee workshops grew high double digit in Q2. Company has about 7,000 OEM franchisee workshops.

segments.name: Lubricants - B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial B2B grew high double digit in Q2; nearly one-third of incremental growth came from new customers. B2C/B2B mix was roughly 50:50 in Q2 vs a historical 55:45.

segments.name: Lubricants - B2C (channel)
segments.commentary: B2C grew about 2x the market in H1 per management; outlets grew 16% YoY. Management targets at least 2x market growth going forward.

segments.name: AdBlue
segments.commentary: Q2 volume of 33,000 KL was lower on monsoon-related lower truck movement; H1 about 73,000 KL, roughly flat. Guidance is double-digit (10-15%) growth going forward.

segments.name: Tirex (EV chargers)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue of INR 33 crore+, up 78% YoY. Capacity to rise to 3,000 chargers by end of this year; the Chennai/plant expansion targeted for the coming quarter.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27: management expects the industry to grow about 3-4% and Gulf to grow 2x-3x that, implying close to double-digit volume growth in H2. Agri demand is currently weak.
Margin: medium-term trajectory back to 14-16% EBITDA margin, but management said this is not a 1-2 quarter story; focus is on per-litre margin protection.
Pricing: base oil has not yet shown the recent crude rally ($100 to $115); if crude sustains, price hikes segment-wise may follow in about 40-50 days. Base oil inventory held for 45-60 days.
Working capital: management said the current level is near peak if prices hold; incremental H2 cash generation should flow to cash flow rather than working capital.

Capex: Chennai expansion on track for completion by end of the quarter. Silvassa expansion may slip 1-2 months into Q1 FY28 (earlier target March 2027). Total expansion capex now about INR 60-62 crore (from INR 55 crore).
Dividend: payout raised to around 65-70% last year; management indicated cash returns depend on M&A and reinvestment opportunities.

Personal mobility: about 21% of volume; passenger car (PCMO) share below 5%, target to add 3-4% to personal mobility mix, largely from cars. Synthetic range target about 10% of portfolio over 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Chennai plant capacity expansion on track; increased capacity expected by end of Q3 FY27 (end of this quarter).
Silvassa capacity expansion may slip 1-2 months; readiness now expected in Q1 FY28 vs March 2027 target. Third shifts running at both plants.
Total expansion capex now about INR 60-62 crore (INR 55 crore earlier plus INR 5-7 crore incremental sanctioned by the Board).
Tirex capacity to be raised to 3,000 chargers by end of this year; plant expansion targeted to be complete in the coming quarter.
Valsad fire: about 4-5 days of production lost in inventory terms; stocks insured; extra shifts planned. 25 warehouses across India operational.
demand_pricing: Volume growth driven by OEM, franchisee workshops and B2B industrial; supply security was a focus given input supply challenges.

Price increases taken in calibrated fashion: 3 price increases taken in channel (B2C) so far; OEM contracts have quarterly price variation clauses, with monthly variations during the last 6 months; B2B requires negotiation and takes longer.
Exports about 10% of lubes business, up in the last six months on global supply-demand conditions.
Market share about 7-8% of total lubricant market; OMCs make up 30-35% of the market and are expanding base oil capacity.
Base oil and sea freight costs rising due to the Strait of Hormuz disruption; most purchases are CIF/CFR so freight is built into base oil cost per management.
Personal mobility about 21% of volume; PCMO passenger car share below 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise in H1, and will working capital keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute values rose on higher prices, but days remain within the 95-105 day band; the current level is near peak if prices hold, with moderation expected if price increases slow.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of the Valsad fire loss and P&L impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocks are insured. About 4-5 days of equivalent production was lost; extra shifts and inventory moves from other warehouses mean no expected customer disruption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expected to grow 3-4% in H2; Gulf targets 2x-3x that, implying close to double-digit volume growth. Agri demand is weak currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will a crude rise be passed on, and when could margins return to 14-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Base oil has not yet moved with the $100-$115 crude rally; price actions would follow if crude sustains. Medium-term return to 14-16% is the aim, but not in one or two quarters; management is protecting per-litre margin.

qa_highlights.question: How are dividends, cash of INR 1,200 crore and M&A planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is earmarked as a war chest for lubricant-space M&A, industrial and mobility adjacencies including EV value chain; payout raised to about 65-70%, with returns to shareholders when surplus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex status and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai on track for end-quarter; Silvassa may slip to Q1 FY28. Total expansion capex about INR 60-62 crore.

risks_watch: Base oil lag: crude rally to $100-$115 not yet in base oil; a sustained crude rise could force further price hikes or squeeze margins.
Working capital and cash conversion: low EBITDA-to-CFO conversion in H1 for the second year; management says near peak but depends on prices.
Silvassa expansion delay into Q1 FY28 could constrain supply if demand strengthens.
Weak agri demand in the current month; H2 double-digit volume growth depends on festive and industrial demand.
Inventory adjustments in the consolidated P&L rose to INR 109 crore (Q1) and INR 88 crore (Q2); management attributes this to price and tactical buying.
Valsad fire and possible supply disruption; insured but operational risk remains.
Passenger car share below 5%; the personal mobility growth target depends on this segment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and market share, with the 2x-3x market growth target repeated. Cautious and somewhat evasive on margin outlook, pricing action and base oil trajectory, repeatedly deferring to per-litre margin protection. Declined to quantify cumulative price increases or competitor pricing gaps.

We have to be very pragmatic in that.

adds.what: Tirex EV charger capacity to 3,000 chargers by end FY27

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 lube volume at 2x-3x the 3-4% industry growth (near double-digit), backed by Chennai capacity due by end of Q3 FY27, Silvassa expansion slipping to Q1 FY28, and third shifts at both plants; Q2 core lube volume rose ~16% with revenue +44%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 11.8% vs 12-14% guided band; medium-term aim 14-16%, but management says it is not a 1-2 quarter story and base oil has not yet absorbed the $100-$115 crude rally.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chennai expansion on track for end of this quarter (Q3 FY27) and Silvassa slipping 1-2 months into Q1 FY28 from March 2027; third shifts already running at both plants, and Tirex goes to 3,000 chargers by end FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides Gulf at 2x-3x the 3-4% industry growth, implying close to double-digit H2 volume, after Q2 core lube volume rose 16% to 47,000 KL and H1 rose 17%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Expansion capex already raised to INR 60-62 crore from INR 55 crore, and INR 1,200 crore cash is earmarked for lubricant-space M&A and adjacencies, but no new plant is announced and utilisation was not quantified (third shifts running).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the H2 2x-3x industry growth view and the 14-16% medium-term margin, and did not signal raising guidance while crude and base oil costs are rising.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Weak agri demand now, Silvassa slipping to Q1 FY28, Valsad fire costing 4-5 days of production, and base oil lag to crude, with H2 double-digit growth dependent on festive and industrial demand.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new lubricant product launch was named; synthetic range target of about 10% of portfolio is over 3-4 years.

rows.label: Price hikes if crude sustains
rows.why: Base oil has not yet shown the $100-$115 crude rally; 3 channel price increases taken so far, and segment-wise hikes may follow if crude holds.

rows.label: Working capital near peak
rows.why: Management says working capital is near peak if prices hold, with H2 cash generation expected to flow to cash flow; days within 95-105 band.

rows.label: Personal mobility mix up 3-4 points
rows.why: Personal mobility is about 21% of volume and PCMO share is below 5%; target to add 3-4% to mix, largely from cars, is a multi-year aim.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume, market share and the 2x-3x industry growth target, but cautious and deferential on margin recovery, base oil and price action; analysts pressed on margin timing and working capital.
